selection_rule: Data-type hints propose readings; scientific roles and study design require explicit evidence.

options.reading_task: Read the spread, skew and raw observations of a measurement
options.mapping_status: candidate; confirm field meanings before plotting

methods_to_consider_after_design: welch or mannwhitney for independent two-group questions
paired_t or wilcoxon for explicitly paired two-condition questions
questions: What does one row represent, and which column identifies the independently sampled unit?
What do the selected measurements mean, and what are their units?
Are observations independent, paired, or repeated within a unit?
Which comparisons were intended, and which missing-value tokens and exclusions are valid?

notes: Display raw observations and summary definitions explicitly; an observed row is not automatically a biological replicate.

options.reading_task: Read whether two supplied numeric measurements vary together
options.mapping_status: candidate; confirm field meanings before plotting

methods_to_consider_after_design: pearson for an adopted linear association question
spearman for an adopted monotonic association question
questions: What does one row represent, and which column identifies the independently sampled unit?
What do the selected measurements mean, and what are their units?
Are observations independent, paired, or repeated within a unit?
Which comparisons were intended, and which missing-value tokens and exclusions are valid?
Are scales or transformations required, and does each unit contribute one independent pair?

notes: A scatter preview does not establish causation or justify a fitted curve.

options.reading_task: Check whether an explicit unit has measurements in multiple conditions

questions: Does this identifier refer to the same unit across conditions?
Is there one value per unit and condition, or are technical repeats present?
How should unmatched units be handled without silently dropping them?

notes: Matching-looking identifiers are a candidate relationship; the command has not established or created pairs.
